RCC Automated Payroll System (RCC-APS) : An Integrated Web Solution for Automated Labor Law Compliance and Payroll Analytics

This capstone project entitled “RCC Automated Payroll System (RCC-APS): An Integrated Web Solution for Automated Labor Law Compliance and Payroll Analytics,” prepared and presented by Batuaan, Jhon Gerald, Cabigting, John Carlo, and Valencia, Rick Nash, in partial fulfillment of the requirements for the degree Bachelor of Science in Information Technology, has been reviewed and is hereby recommended for approval and acceptance.
Approved by the Panel of Examiners:
Accepted and approved in partial fulfillment of the requirements for the degree Bachelor of Science in Information Technology.

The researchers would like to express their sincerest gratitude and appreciation to all the individuals and institutions who contributed to the successful completion of this capstone project. Their guidance, support, and encouragement were invaluable throughout the development of the RCC Automated Payroll System.

The RCC-APS or Republic Central Colleges Automated Payroll System is a web-based payroll management system developed for Republic Central Colleges. It is designed to automate the computation of employee salaries, mandatory government deductions, and net pay, providing a modern, automated, and legally compliant payroll solution for the institution.The system is built for three types of users. The Finance Officer uses the system to process the monthly payroll, generate payslips, and produce financial reports. The Regular Employee uses the Employee Dashboard to view and download their digital payslips and update their personal contact information. The System Administrator manages all user accounts and role assignments within the system.The RCC-APS is developed using the following technologies: Vanilla JavaScript for the frontend user interface, Node.js with Express.js for the backend server and API, MySQL for the database, and JWT (JSON Web Tokens) for secure authentication and role-based access control. The system is developed following the Agile software development methodology.The system automatically computes the Gross Pay, SSS contribution, PhilHealth premium, Pag-IBIG contribution, BIR withholding tax under the TRAIN Law, and the final Net Pay of each employee, all in compliance with Philippine labor and tax regulations.

Payroll management is one of the most fundamental administrative functions in any organization. It involves the systematic computation of employee wages, application of mandatory government deductions, and timely delivery of accurate compensation. According to the Society for Human Resource Management

, organizations that implement automated payroll solutions experience a significant reduction in processing time and human error rates compared to less automated approaches. Effective payroll systems not only ensure accurate compensation but also reinforce employee trust and institutional compliance.

In the Philippine context, payroll management carries additional complexity due to government-mandated contribution programs that every employer must comply with. These include the Social Security System (SSS) under Republic Act No. 11199
, the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) under Republic Act No. 11223
, the Home Development Mutual Fund or Pag-IBIG under Republic Act No. 9679
, and the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) withholding tax under the TRAIN Law or Republic Act No. 10963

. Each of these agencies prescribes specific contribution rates and computation rules that must be accurately applied in every payroll cycle. Non-compliance results in penalties, back payments, and reputational damage to the institution.
Several studies have demonstrated the benefits of automating payroll and administrative processes in institutional settings.

noted that even automated systems, if not properly designed, can suffer from poor data accuracy and limited analytical capabilities, highlighting the importance of well-engineered payroll solutions. Research by
further emphasized that automation reduces administrative workload and minimizes the risk of errors in government contribution computations — a critical concern for Philippine institutions.
Role-based access control (RBAC), as described by the National Institute of Standards and Technology

, is recognized as a security best practice for enterprise information systems. By restricting access to system features based on user roles, RBAC ensures data integrity, reduces unauthorized access risk, and promotes accountability. Commercial payroll platforms available in the Philippines, such as Sprout Solutions and GreatDay HR

, demonstrate that this principle is widely applied in modern payroll systems. However, these commercial solutions are primarily designed for large enterprises and may not fully address the specific operational context of an educational institution such as Republic Central Colleges.

A review of related capstone and academic projects on payroll automation in Philippine institutions reveals common limitations — most student-developed systems lack full compliance with the BIR TRAIN Law tax schedule, do not integrate with a separate Human Resource Information System (HRIS), or are limited to a single user type without differentiated access controls. These gaps indicate a clear opportunity to develop a more comprehensive, legally compliant, and institutionally tailored payroll solution.
Guided by these findings and the established importance of accurate payroll management, this capstone project developed the
RCC-APS: Republic Central Colleges Automated Payroll System

— a web-based payroll management system designed to provide Republic Central Colleges with a modern, automated, and legally compliant payroll solution. The RCC-APS was built to deliver the following outputs for the institution: automated payroll computation covering Gross Pay, all mandatory government deductions, and Net Pay; digital payslip generation and PDF download for employees; payroll summary and contribution reports for the Finance Officer; role-based access control for three user classes; and a deduction table management module for maintaining updated government contribution rates.

By developing the RCC-APS, this project seeks to contribute a purpose-built, institution-specific solution that addresses the payroll management needs of Republic Central Colleges, while serving as a practical demonstration of the knowledge and skills developed by the team throughout their academic program.

The general objective of this study is to design, develop, and evaluate a web-based automated payroll system for Republic Central Colleges that accurately computes employee salaries, mandatory government deductions, and net pay in compliance with Philippine labor and tax laws.

The development of the RCC-APS is significant to the following stakeholders:

The system directly relieves Finance Officers of payroll computation responsibilities by automating the calculation of Gross Pay, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, BIR withholding tax, and Net Pay. This eliminates human error, significantly reduces processing time, and ensures that all computations are fully compliant with Philippine government regulations.

Employees benefit from a transparent, self-service Employee Dashboard that allows them to view and download their payslips at any time. This eliminates the need to request physical copies from the Finance department and gives employees full visibility into how their take-home pay was computed, promoting trust and transparency.

The System Administrator gains a centralized User Management Panel to create, remove, deactivate, and reactivate user accounts and assign user roles. This ensures that system access is always controlled and current, particularly when employees join and leave, within the organization.

The institution benefits from a more efficient, legally compliant, and error-free payroll process. The RCC-APS reduces the administrative workload of the Finance department, minimizes the risk of regulatory penalties from government agencies, and presents a modern and technology-driven approach to institutional management.

This project provides Batuaan, Jhon Gerald; Cabigting, John; and Valencia, Nash with practical, hands-on experience in the full software development lifecycle — from requirements analysis and system design through Agile development, testing, and documentation — demonstrating their competencies as graduating BSIT students.

The RCC-APS serves as a reference and foundation for future capstone projects and academic research in payroll automation, HRIS integration, and role-based web application development in the Philippine educational context. Its documentation, architecture, and compliance approach can guide subsequent development teams in extending or building upon this work.

This section describes the scope of the RCC-APS and clarifies its intentional exclusions. It assists stakeholders in forming accurate expectations about the system's purpose, coverage, and limitations.
The RCC-APS covers the following functionalities:
User authentication and role-based access control for three distinct user classes: Finance Officer, Regular Employee, and System Administrator, each with a dedicated dashboard and feature set;

Payroll computation including Gross Pay calculation, automatic deduction of SSS contributions (based on the official salary bracket table), PhilHealth premium (5% of basic monthly salary, 2.5% employee share), Pag-IBIG contributions (2% of monthly compensation, capped at ₱100.00 per month), BIR withholding tax (computed using the TRAIN Law annual tax schedule), and final Net Pay;
Digital payslip generation with a detailed breakdown of earnings and deductions, and employee-accessible PDF download;
Government contribution and payroll summary report generation with export functionality in PDF format;
User account management including creation, removing, deactivation, and reactivation of system accounts by the System Administrator;
Deduction table management allowing the Finance Officer to update SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and BIR contribution rates; and
Integration with the partner HRIS system for receiving employee data and deduction rate inputs.
The following are outside the scope of the RCC-APS:
The system does not process actual bank transfers, e-wallet disbursements, or any form of salary payment transaction;
Employee attendance tracking, biometric integration, and time-keeping are not handled by the RCC-APS. These functions remain within the scope of the partner HRIS system;
Overtime filing, approval, and overtime pay computation are not included in the system's scope;
Employee hiring, recruitment, onboarding, and scheduling are managed by the HRIS and are entirely outside the scope of the RCC-APS; and
The system does not replicate or replace the full functionality of the HRIS. It only receives input data from the HRIS and does not write back to it.

This section presents and interprets the key outcomes of the RCC-APS based on the methodology described in the preceding chapter. It discusses how the completed system meets each of the objectives of the study, presents the sample outputs produced by the system, and highlights the insights and issues encountered during the development process. Detailed outputs, screenshots, and other supporting materials may be found in the Project Artifacts section.

All six modules of the RCC-APS — the Login Module (M1), User Management Module (M2), Payroll Calculation Module (M3), Employee Dashboard Module (M4), Reporting Module (M5), and Deduction Table Management Module (M6) — were successfully designed, developed, integrated, and tested within the six Agile sprints described in the methodology. The completed application runs as a single-page web application built with Vanilla JavaScript (HTML5, CSS3, and custom CSS), supported by a Node.js and Express.js backend connected to a MySQL database, with JWT-based authentication and role-based access control for the three user classes. Screenshots of the implemented modules are presented in the Project Artifacts section.

The Payroll Calculation Engine (M3) was validated against the official SSS salary credit table (Republic Act No. 11199), the 5% PhilHealth premium rate with a 2.5% employee share (Republic Act No. 11223), the Pag-IBIG contribution computed at 2% of monthly compensation and capped at ₱100.00 (Republic Act No. 9679), and the BIR withholding tax schedule under the TRAIN Law (Republic Act No. 10963). Each computation formula produced results that matched the manual computations performed using the official contribution tables.

Table 1 shows the monthly deductions and net pay computed by the system for the three active demo employees for the December 2026 payroll period. The BIR withholding tax was annualized on the monthly taxable income — the gross pay minus the employee’s mandatory SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG contributions — consistent with the annualization rules under BIR Revenue Regulations No. 11-2018.

For example, Jhon Gerald Batuaan with a monthly salary of ₱28,500.00 incurs an SSS contribution of ₱1,425.00 (₱28,250.00 – ₱28,749.00 bracket), a PhilHealth premium of ₱712.50, and a Pag-IBIG contribution of ₱00.00, resulting in a monthly taxable income of ₱26,262.50. Annualized, this amounts to ₱315,150.00, which falls within the 15% withholding bracket, producing an annual withholding tax of ₱9,772.50, or ₱814.38 per month, and a final net pay of ₱25,448.12. Nash Valencia and John Cabigting, whose annual taxable incomes exceed the ₱250,000.00 exemption threshold, were correctly withheld at the applicable rates.

Every computed result was compared against the corresponding manual calculation performed using the official government tables. All figures matched to the centavo, confirming the accuracy and compliance of the Payroll Calculation Engine.
13th Month Pay and Bonus Compliance Results

The system computed the 13th month pay in accordance with Republic Act No. 8515, applying a pro-rated amount based on the months of service actually rendered during the year, and withheld the statutory excess tax on the 13th month pay and taxable bonuses in accordance with the ₱90,000.00 annual exemption provided under the TRAIN Law (Republic Act No. 10963, as amended by the CREATE Act). In the December 2026 payroll run, all demo employees remained within the ₱90,000.00 exemption, so their full 13th month pay was released tax-free. The system correctly identified any employee whose 13th month pay and taxable bonuses exceeded the exemption threshold and computed the corresponding excess withholding tax, which was applied in full to the December pay.

The Employee Dashboard Module (M4) successfully generated digital payslips containing a complete breakdown of gross pay, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, BIR withholding tax, 13th month pay, and net pay for each payroll period. Regular employees were able to view and download their payslips as PDF files through the Employee Dashboard and to update their personal contact information. Access to these features was restricted to the Regular Employee role, as defined by the role-based access control configuration.

The Reporting Module (M5) enabled the Finance Officer to generate a payroll summary report and a government contribution report for a selected month and year. The reports correctly aggregated the gross pay and the SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and BIR withholding tax of all employees, and the column totals were verified to equal the sum of the corresponding individual payroll records. Both reports were successfully exported to PDF.
User Management and Deduction Table Management Results

Through the User Management Module (M2), the System Administrator was able to create, update, deactivate, and reactivate user accounts and assign user roles. Role-based access control prevented each user class from accessing functions outside its assigned role. Through the Deduction Table Management Module (M6), the Finance Officer was able to update the SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and BIR contribution tables directly through the system interface; the updated rates were applied to the payroll computations immediately without requiring any modification to the source code.

The testing procedures described in the methodology were executed and produced the following results. Unit testing of the Payroll Calculation Engine confirmed that each formula — the SSS bracket lookup, PhilHealth rate application, Pag-IBIG cap enforcement, BIR TRAIN Law annualization, and Net Pay derivation — matched the manually computed expected values based on the official government tables. Integration testing confirmed the data flow from the MySQL database through the REST API to the calculation engine, from the calculation engine to payslip generation, and from the Reporting Module to the export functionality, and all REST API endpoints were verified . System testing confirmed the stability and correct behavior of the complete system in an operational environment. User Acceptance Testing was conducted with simulated end users representing the Finance Officer, Regular Employee, and System Administrator, and all defined acceptance criteria were met. Performance and security testing confirmed responsive payroll processing and report generation, and the protection of payroll data, employee records, and authentication tokens from unauthorized access. Regression testing was performed after every bug fix and confirmed that previously working features, particularly in the calculation engine, remained functional.

Several insights and issues were encountered during the development and testing of the system. First, the team initially computed the BIR withholding tax on the full gross monthly pay. During testing, it was identified that BIR Revenue Regulations No. 11-2018 requires the withholding tax to be computed on the monthly taxable income, which is the gross pay minus the employee’s mandatory SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG contributions. The calculation engine was corrected accordingly, and the correction was verified across all test cases. Second, government contribution rates change periodically; this finding motivated the development of the Deduction Table Management Module so that updated rates can be applied without modifying the source code. Third, because the application persists all records in a centralized MySQL database accessed through the server’s REST API, employees and the Finance Officer always see consistent, up-to-date data regardless of the device or browser they use. Data consistency is therefore maintained centrally on the server rather than on the client.
Summary of Results against the Objectives of the Study

The results of the project satisfy all of the objectives of the study. First, the system automatically computes the Gross Pay, government deductions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and BIR withholding tax), and Net Pay of each employee in compliance with the Social Security Act of 2018, the Universal Health Care Act, the HDMF Law, and the TRAIN Law. Second, a secure role-based web application provides distinct dashboards for the Finance Officer, Regular Employee, and System Administrator. Third, digital payslip generation and PDF download are accessible through the Employee Dashboard. Fourth, the Reporting Module generates payroll summary reports and government contribution reports and exports them in PDF format. Fifth, the Deduction Table Management Module allows the Finance Officer to update government contribution rates without modifying the system’s source code. Sixth, employee records and deduction rate inputs are persisted in a centralized MySQL database and accessed through REST API endpoints, keeping the data consistent across all users of the system. Finally, the accuracy, usability, and functionality of the system were evaluated through unit, integration, system, performance, security, and regression testing, as well as user acceptance testing conducted with simulated end users for each user class.
The detailed outputs, screenshots, and other supporting materials for the results discussed in this section are presented in the Project Artifacts section.
This chapter presents the discussion of the results of the study, the conclusions drawn from the findings, and the recommendations for the future improvement and extension of the RCC-APS.

The results presented in the preceding chapter demonstrate that the RCC-APS successfully fulfills the objectives of the study. The Payroll Calculation Engine produced deductions that matched the manual computations performed against the official government contribution tables, confirming the compliance of the system with the Social Security Act of 2018, the Universal Health Care Act, the HDMF Law, and the TRAIN Law. In particular, the correction of the BIR withholding tax computation from the full gross pay to the monthly taxable income — the gross pay minus the mandatory SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG contributions — aligned the system with the annualization rules under BIR Revenue Regulations No. 11-2018, and the consistent results across all test cases validated the reliability of the calculation engine. The role-based dashboards for the three user classes, the digital payslip generation with PDF download, the payroll summary and government contribution reports, and the configurable deduction tables all functioned as designed. The results of the unit, integration, system, performance, security, and regression tests, as well as the user acceptance testing conducted with simulated end users, confirmed the accuracy, usability, and functionality of the system. These findings are consistent with the review of related literature, which emphasized that automation reduces processing time and human error and that role-based access control improves security and accountability. The system likewise addresses the gaps identified among related capstone projects by implementing full compliance with the BIR TRAIN Law tax schedule, a dedicated deduction table management module, and differentiated access controls for three user classes.

Based on the findings of the study, the following conclusions are drawn. The RCC-APS successfully automates the computation of the Gross Pay, the mandatory government deductions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and BIR withholding tax), and the Net Pay of each employee in compliance with the applicable Philippine labor and tax laws. The system provides a secure, role-based web application with distinct dashboards for the Finance Officer, Regular Employee, and System Administrator, effectively enforcing role-based access control across all features. The digital payslip generation and PDF download feature provides employees with transparent, self-service access to their compensation records. The Reporting Module enables the Finance Officer to generate payroll summary reports and government contribution reports and to export them in PDF format. The Deduction Table Management Module allows the Finance Officer to update government contribution rates without modifying the system’s source code. The centralized MySQL database and REST API endpoints keep the data consistent across all users of the system. The accuracy, usability, and functionality of the system were validated through unit, integration, system, performance, security, and regression testing, as well as through user acceptance testing conducted with simulated end users for each user class. Overall, the study concludes that the RCC-APS is a functional, accurate, and legally compliant payroll solution tailored to the operational context of Republic Central Colleges.

The following recommendations are offered for the future improvement and extension of the RCC-APS. First, the BIR withholding tax computation should be continuously monitored against amendments to the TRAIN Law and its implementing regulations, and the annualized taxable income method should be retained and periodically revalidated. Second, the integration with the partner HRIS should be extended to automate the import of attendance, overtime, and employee data, thereby reducing manual data entry. Third, the MySQL database schema could be expanded to support additional statutory deductions, loan amortizations, and other benefits, further strengthening concurrency, data consistency, and compliance coverage. Fourth, the system could incorporate additional statutory benefits and deductions — such as SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG loan amortizations, withholding tax on other compensation, and other government-mandated contributions — to further expand its compliance coverage. Fifth, automated testing should be expanded to cover the reporting and user management modules, and the test suite should be maintained alongside future system changes. Sixth, actual institutional deployment with the Finance Office of Republic Central Colleges is recommended to validate the system under real payroll conditions. Finally, future researchers may build upon this study by evaluating the system through formal usability studies and by exploring the integration of the RCC-APS with other institutional systems.

This market research examines the existing payroll solutions used and developed by academic institutions in the Philippines. It compares open-source and documented systems built for colleges and universities with the RCC-APS Automated Payroll System of Republic Central Colleges (RCC). The purpose is to identify the strengths and limitations of existing solutions and to position RCC-APS as a tailored alternative for RCC.
The specific objectives of this research are to:
identify the payroll solutions currently used or developed in academic institutions;
compare their features against those of the RCC-APS system;
determine the gaps left by existing solutions; and
highlight the unique advantages of RCC-APS that answer the question, “What is unique about this system compared to other payroll systems?”

In many educational institutions in the Philippines, payroll is still processed through manual records, paper forms, or spreadsheet software such as Microsoft Excel. Schools use a mix of full-time (non-teaching) staff and teaching personnel who are compensated by hourly load. As a result, payroll is repetitive, prone to human error, and time-consuming.

Several colleges and universities have responded by developing their own automated payroll systems. These systems vary in technology, security, and functionality. This research reviews three such systems and a manual baseline, comparing them with the RCC-APS system to show how RCC-APS addresses the specific needs of an academic institution.

6. UNIQUENESS OF RCC-APS: WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
The following points summarize why the RCC-APS Automated Payroll System stands out from other payroll systems.
RCC-APS is purposely designed for Republic Central Colleges. It is not a generic product modified to fit a school; it is built around the exact payroll structure of RCC.
The system natively supports two compensation models: Teaching personnel paid by hours worked, and Non-Teaching personnel paid a fixed monthly salary with absences deducted over 22 working days.
RCC-APS connects to the RCC HRIS to automatically compute teaching hours and detect absences (no clock-in and no approved leave = absent), reducing manual data entry.
SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and BIR withholding tables are built in and editable, keeping the system compliant with Philippine law without manual rate lookup.
Employees can view and download their digital payslips, and the finance officer can generate reports and analytics in minutes.
The primary target market of RCC-APS is Republic Central Colleges, specifically its System Administrator, Finance Officer, and employees who rely on timely and accurate payroll.

A secondary market includes other colleges and educational institutions in the Philippines that employ both hourly teaching and salaried non-teaching personnel and wish to automate their payroll while maintaining compliance with Philippine statutory requirements.

Existing payroll solutions fall short in addressing the specific needs of an academic institution: they are either error-prone (manual), limited in statutory handling, or designed for a different institution. The RCC-APS Automated Payroll System fills this gap by providing an accurate, compliant, and tailor-fit payroll solution for Republic Central Colleges, giving it a clear and defensible unique advantage in the market.
